chapter.title_hebrew: הענף הה': סיכום וחיזוק דעת הגאונים
chapter.title_english: Branch Five: Summary and Reinforcement of the Geonic View

paragraphs.hebrew_raw: הקדוש, וכמ"ש, כתב התשב"ץ בח"ב סי' ח"ל ד"י ע"א וז"ל: "ואיני חושב שתהא שאלתך על זה! שלא' נתן לנו היום לפסוק במחלוקת הגמרא כלום כי כבר מתוקן הוא בפסקי הראשונים והאחרונים" עכ"ד ועיין לו עוד בח"א סי' קנ"ג ד"ה והשלישי, ובח"ג סי' מ"ה כתב, דקבלת הגאונים קבלה היא וראוי לסמוך עליהם כאלו נזכר בתלמוד, ודבר זה ידוע לתלמידי דבי רב שאפי' על ר"ח ראשון לרבנים, מפני שינק מהגאונים נאמר עליו "כל דבריו דברי קבלה" ועיין ש"ך יו"ד סי' כ"ה סק"ב שכתב "דכמה פעמים מצינו שהתוספות והראשונים חששו לדברי בעל ה"ג, אפי' היכא דלא מסתבר טעמיה, ואפי' להקל מפני שכל דבריו ד"ק, עכ"ד. וכ"כ לקמן סימן קצ"ח סק"ך, לענין נדר עיש"ב באומרו: "אפילו שלא נמצא בש"ס שלנו, מ"מ דברי ב"הג דברי קבלה הם" ע"כ. הרי להדיא שמפני שהגאונים דבריהם דברי קבלה, ע"ז סמכינן עלייהו, אפי' דלא מסתבר טעמייהו, ואפי' להקל, וריא"ז עצמו שחלק על הגאונים מפני שהיו דברי נביאות לעקור שיטת התלמוד וכנז"ל, איהו גופיה כתב ה"ד הריקאנטי"סו"סי פ"ח: "דאע"ג דמכח הגמרא לא משמע הכי, אין לנו כח לחלוק ע"ד הקדמונים" ומה לנו עוד רבות דברים, אחרי שרבינו שרירא ז"ל, בהדיא קאמר לה בתשובה זאת, שלפנינו באומרו: "וחכמת הגאונים ופלפוליהם הוא הדבר אשר צוה ה' אל משה ואע"פ שאומרים כן ואין מביאין ראיה באיזה מקום הוא אין לחוש וכו' וכל החולק וכו' מבואר לעין כל דלא אמר הגאון, וכו' החולק וכו' אלא על חי' הדינים והפלפולים שאין מביאין ראיה באיזה מקום הוא, ולא על איזה דברים, כי נער כתבם, המנגדים על שרשי הגמ' חלילה! לגאון אדיר כר"ש שיאמר כן! ועיין תשב"ץ ח"ב סי' נ"ד שכתב וז"ל "הזמן מספיק להוצאת האמת, והרי כמה שנים גודלנו בב"המ ולא נגלה לנו טעמו של הרמב"ם במה שפסק וכו', ועכשיו נתגלה לנו טעמו" עיש"ב. ואני במקומי סיימתי אחר דבריו אלה וכתבתי: ומכל זה ישמע חכם ויוסף לקח שלא לחלוק על הראשונים, ע"כ דברי, וא"כ שפיר קאמר רב שרירא ז"ל שאין לחלוק עליהם, מפני שלא הביאו ראיה לדבריהם, דאפשר מאיזה מקור חצבו דבריהם ואנן לא בקיאינן בגויה, ובפרט ביודעינו ומכירנו כמה גניזות וכמה מסכתות שלמות היו בידם ונאבדו מאתנו, הא ודאי כל החולק עליהם כחולק על ה', ומה לי להאריך עוד, אחרי שמוהר"ם אלאשקר בסי' ג"ן שניטפל בבירור דבר זה על מתכונתו, ר"ל על מי נאמר הלכה כבתראי ועל מי לא, ועל מה נסמוך על הגאונים. ועל מה לא, כבר חוטף החרב חדה הזאת מיד התלמידים שלא שמשו כל צרכם, במה שברר הדברים יפה יפה כאיש גבורתו, ונסתייע מתשו' זאת אשר לפנינו, ובריש ס' שערי צדק, שהיתה בידו כ"י וביאר עליה הדברים כנתינתן, וע"ז צויתי להעתיק שורות אחרונות אלו הבאות בתשו' גאוננו ז"ל באותיות גדולות, כלומר, הרי שורות אחרונות אלו, הנראות בהשקפה ראשונה, כאלו רב שרירא הוא המגדיל המדורה ומעלה תורת הגאונים לשמי השמים העליונים, עד שהחכם השד"ל נר"ו לא מצא תרופה למכה זאת, כי אם לטעון טענת זיוף כדי להציל לרש"ג ז"ל מפי אריות, הרי שורות אחרונות אלו, קרואות והולכות לתומם, בס' קדמון אשר מחברו חי זה קרוב לד' מאות שנה, ובחכמתו ואמונתו הרמה, חזקם ואמצם ובררם כשמלה, וסיים להחזיקם בדברי הראב"ד שכתב: "דאין מי שיוכל לחלוק על דברי גאון ואפילו שלא יביא ראיה לדבריו, והחולק עליו כחולק על התלמוד" וסיים וכתב וז"ל: "והנה כמה פעמים אנו רואים לגדולי אחרונים עצמן שמבטלים דעתם מפני דעתם של ראשונים, ואומרים, אעפ"י שאין נראה כן מן הגמ' שלנו ומן הירושלמי, אחר שיצא הדבר מפי פלוני, אנו מבטלין דעתנו מפני דעתו, כמו שכתבו הרשב"א והר"ן וזולתן לגבי הרי"ף וכו' וכל ספרי האחרונים מלאים מכיוצא בזה" א"ד, עיש"ב ועתה סמוך להדפסה קניתי שאר חלקי בכורי העתים בקמ"ד ווין ע"א מפני תורתו של ידידינו הגאון שי"ר נר"ו דחביבה עלי עד לאחת, וראיתי לו שם בב"הע תקצ"א עמוד פ"ד שכתב על רבינו שרירא ז"ל שהוא "מתאמץ ג"כ לרומם כל פסקי הגאונים ולהעלות כל דבריהם בעיני החכמים כמו דברי חז"ל בתלמוד" והעתיק תשו' שלפנינו דעיקר מטרין עלה כמו שהובאה בריש ס' תשו' שערי צדק אות באות כולה בכתב רש"י, וכשהגיע לתיבות, "וחכמתם ופלפוליהם הוא הדבר אשר צוה ה', העתיקם בכתב אשורית, וכן מתיבות "כל החולק על שום דבר מדבריהם כחולק על ה' ועל תורתו"

paragraphs.english_raw: The Holy One. And as is written, the Tashbetz wrote in Volume Two, Responsum Thirty-Eight, folio fourteen, column one, and his words are as follows: "And I do not believe that your question concerns this! For it has not been granted to us today to render a Halakhic decision concerning any dispute in the Gemara, for it has already been clarified in the rulings of the Rishonim and the Acharonim." Thus far his words. And see for him further in Volume One, Responsum One Hundred Fifty-Three, under the heading "And the third." And in Volume Three, Responsum Forty-Five, he wrote that the tradition of the Ge'onim is an accepted tradition, and it is proper to rely upon them as if it were stated in the Talmud. And this matter is known to the students of the Rabbinic academy, that even concerning Rabbenu Chananel, the foremost of the Rabbanim, because he drew from the Ge'onim, it was said concerning him: "All his words are words of tradition." And see the Siftei Kohen in Yoreh De'ah, Chapter Twenty-Five, sub-paragraph Two, who wrote: "For how many times do we find that the Tosafot and the Rishonim took into account the words of the Ba'al Halakhot Gedolot, even where his reasoning was not persuasive, and even to be lenient, because all his words are words of tradition." Thus far his words. And so he wrote further on, in Chapter One Hundred Ninety-Eight, sub-paragraph Twenty, concerning a vow, see there, where he states: "Even if it is not found in our Talmud, nevertheless, the words of the Ba'al Halakhot Gedolot are words of tradition." End of quote.

paragraphs.english_raw: Behold, it is clear that because the words of the Ge'onim are words of tradition, we rely upon them for this, even if their reasoning is not persuasive, and even to be lenient. And Rabbi Yitzchak ben Reuven Albarceloni himself, who disagreed with the Ge'onim because they were prophetic words seeking to uproot the method of the Talmud, as mentioned above, he himself wrote in the Recanati, section eighty-eight: "For even though it is not implied thus from the Gemara, we do not have the power to disagree with the words of the early authorities." And what need do we have for further elaboration, after Rabbenu Sherira, of blessed memory, explicitly stated it in this responsum before us, saying: "And the wisdom of the Ge'onim and their dialectics is the matter which the Lord commanded to Moses. And even though they say so and do not bring proof from which place it is, one need not be concerned, etc. And whoever disagrees, etc." It is clear to all that the Gaon did not say, etc., "whoever disagrees, etc.," except concerning novel rulings and dialectics for which no proof is brought from their source, and not concerning certain matters, for a youth wrote them, those who contradict the fundamental principles of the Gemara – Heaven forbid! Far be it from a mighty Gaon like Rabbenu Sherira to say such a thing! And see the Tashbetz, Volume Two, Responsum Fifty, who wrote as follows: "Time is sufficient for the revelation of truth. And behold, for how many years have we grown up in the Bet ha-Midrash, and the reasoning of the Rambam in what he ruled, etc., was not revealed to us, and now his reasoning has been revealed to us." See there. And I, in my place, concluded after these words of his and wrote: "And from all this, a wise person will hear and gain a lesson, not to disagree with the Rishonim." Thus far my words. And if so, Rabbenu Sherira, of blessed memory, rightly states that one should not disagree with them because they did not bring proof for their words, for perhaps from some source they quarried their words, and we are not expert in it. And especially since we know and recognize how many hidden texts and how many complete tractates were in their possession and were lost to us – this is certainly true: whoever disagrees with them is as if he disagrees with the Lord. And why should I further elaborate, after our teacher Rabbi Moshe Alashkar, in Responsum Fifty-Three, dealt with the clarification of this matter in its proper form, that is to say, concerning whom is the Halakhah according to the latter authorities, and concerning whom it is not, and upon what should we rely on the Ge'onim, and upon what not. He has already snatched this sharp sword from the hand of students who have not served their full term, in that he clarified the matters very well, like a man of valor, and he was aided by this responsum before us, and at the beginning of Sefer Sha'arei Tzedek, which was in his possession as a manuscript, and he explained the matters upon it as they were given. And concerning this, I commanded to copy these last lines appearing in the responsum of our Gaon, of blessed memory, in large letters, meaning: Behold, these last lines, which appear at first glance, in which Rabbenu Sherira is the one who magnifies the stringency and elevates the Torah of the Ge'onim to the highest heavens, until the sage Samuel David Luzzatto, may his light shine, found no remedy for this wound except to claim forgery in order to save Rabbenu Sherira Gaon, of blessed memory, from the mouths of lions. Behold, these last lines are read and proceed in their straightforwardness, in an ancient book whose author lived nearly four hundred years ago, and with his wisdom and lofty faith, he strengthened and buttressed them and clarified them like a garment. And he concluded by upholding them with the words of the Ra'avad, who wrote: "That there is no one who can disagree with the words of a Gaon, even if he does not bring proof for his words, and whoever disagrees with him is as if he disagrees with the Talmud." And he concluded and wrote as follows: "And behold, how many times do we see the great Acharonim themselves nullifying their own opinions before the opinions of the Rishonim, and they say, 'Even though it does not appear so from our Gemara or from the Yerushalmi, after the matter has issued from the mouth of so-and-so, we nullify our opinion before his opinion,' as the Rashba and the Ran and others wrote concerning the Rif, etc., and all the books of the Acharonim are full of similar instances." See there. And now, close to printing, I acquired the other parts of *Bikkurei ha-Ittim* in Kaf-Mem-Resh, Vienna, page 71, because of the Torah of our friend, the Gaon, may he live for many good years, which is dear to me beyond all measure. And I saw there in *Bikkurei ha-Ittim*, Year 5591, page 84, where he wrote concerning Rabbenu Sherira, of blessed memory, that he "also strives to elevate all the rulings of the Ge'onim and to raise all their words in the eyes of the sages like the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, in the Talmud." And he copied the responsum before us, the main thrust of which is upon it, as it was brought at the beginning of Sefer Teshuvot Sha'arei Tzedek, letter by letter, all in Rashi script. And when he reached the words, "And their wisdom and dialectics is the matter which the Lord commanded to Moses," he copied them in Assyrian script. And similarly, from the words, "whoever disagrees with any of their words is as if he disagrees with the Lord and His Torah also."

And Rabbi Yitzchak ben Reuven Albarceloni himself, who disagreed with the Ge'onim because they were prophetic words seeking to uproot the method of the Talmud, as mentioned above, he himself wrote in the Recanati, section eighty-eight: "For even though it is not implied thus from the Gemara, we do not have the power to disagree with the words of the early authorities." And what need do we have for further elaboration, after Rabbenu Sherira, of blessed memory, explicitly stated it in this responsum before us, saying: "And the wisdom of the Ge'onim and their dialectics is the matter which the Lord commanded to Moses. And even though they say so and do not bring proof from which place it is, one need not be concerned, etc. And whoever disagrees, etc." It is clear to all that the Gaon did not say, etc., "whoever disagrees, etc.," except concerning novel rulings and dialectics for which no proof is brought from their source, and not concerning certain matters, for a youth wrote them, those who contradict the fundamental principles of the Gemara – Heaven forbid! Far be it from a mighty Gaon like Rabbenu Sherira to say such a thing! And see the Tashbetz, Volume Two, Responsum Fifty, who wrote as follows: "Time is sufficient for the revelation of truth. And behold, for how many years have we grown up in the Bet ha-Midrash, and the reasoning of the Rambam in what he ruled, etc., was not revealed to us, and now his reasoning has been revealed to us." See there. And I, in my place, concluded after these words of his and wrote: "And from all this, a wise person will hear and gain a lesson, not to disagree with the Rishonim." Thus far my words. And if so, Rabbenu Sherira, of blessed memory, rightly states that one should not disagree with them because they did not bring proof for their words, for perhaps from some source they quarried their words, and we are not expert in it. And especially since we know and recognize how many hidden texts and how many complete tractates were in their possession and were lost to us – this is certainly true: whoever disagrees with them is as if he disagrees with the Lord.
